title: Implementing Cloud Security for Data at Rest: Encrypted Volumes with AWS EBS and KMS
objectives: Understand the importance of encrypting data at rest in cloud environments
Configure encrypted volumes using Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) and AWS Key Management Service (KMS)
Integrate KMS keys with IAM roles for seamless encryption and decryption
prerequisites: vvpaa-l001: Identity and Access Management Fundamentals

mission_brief.briefing: Your team has been tasked with securing sensitive data stored in an AWS EC2 instance. The data is currently unencrypted and must be protected from unauthorized access.
rules_of_engagement: Ensure that all data at rest within the EC2 instance is encrypted using industry-standard protocols
Configure IAM roles to integrate with KMS keys for seamless encryption and decryption
Verify that EBS volumes are properly encrypted and accessible only through authorized channels

content.concept: Encrypting data at rest is crucial in cloud environments due to the shared responsibility model. AWS provides services such as Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) for persistent block-level storage and AWS Key Management Service (KMS) for securely storing, managing, and rotating encryption keys.
content.walkthrough: To configure encrypted volumes using EBS and KMS, create an IAM role that integrates with a KMS key. Then, attach the EBS volume to your EC2 instance, specifying the KMS key during creation. Verify that the EBS volume is properly encrypted by checking for the 'encrypted' status in the AWS Management Console.
checkpoints: Verify that the IAM role has been correctly integrated with a KMS key
Ensure that the EBS volume is attached to the correct EC2 instance
Confirm that the EBS volume is properly encrypted
common_mistakes: Forgetting to specify the KMS key during EBS volume creation
Not verifying the encryption status of the EBS volume
Failing to integrate the IAM role with a KMS key

lab.setup: Create an AWS EC2 instance, an IAM role, and an EBS volume. Ensure that the IAM role is integrated with a KMS key.
steps: Login to your AWS account using CLI or Management Console
Create a new IAM role that integrates with a KMS key
Attach the EBS volume to your EC2 instance, specifying the KMS key during creation
Verify that the EBS volume is properly encrypted by checking for the 'encrypted' status in the AWS Management Console
Integrate the IAM role with the KMS key using CLI commands

validate.expected: The EBS volume is encrypted and properly attached to your EC2 instance.

safety: Use the 'default' AWS region for this exercise
Do not delete any existing resources within your account
Verify that you have correctly integrated the IAM role with a KMS key before proceeding

elite_competence.scenario_name: Advanced Cloud Security: Data at Rest Protection

bug_injection.description: The EBS volume is not encrypted due to a missing KMS key specification.

success_criteria.expected_output: The EBS volume is encrypted and properly attached to your EC2 instance.

interrogation_questions: What are the key benefits of encrypting data at rest in cloud environments?
How do you configure IAM roles to integrate with KMS keys for seamless encryption and decryption?
What are common mistakes that can lead to EBS volume encryption failure?

Integrated IAM roles with KMS keys for seamless encryption and decryption
